newsitem.title: USA: Clinton to deliver foreign policy speech in Denver.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to deliver foreign policy speech in Denver.

text.p: President Bill Clinton will deliver a speech on the United States' role in the world in Denver on Thursday before he hosts next weekend's summit of the Group of Seven industrialised nations.

White House spokesman Mike McCurry said the speech would set the context for the summit, which includes Russian President Boris Yeltsin as well as the leaders of Britain, France, Germany, Japan, Italy and Canada.

"The president will give a speech that sort of sets the context for the deliberations that the leaders will have and talk specifically about some of the challenges America faces as it thinks about the global marketplace of the 21st century," McCurry said. He said Clinton had cleared time in his schedule on Friday for private bilateral meetings.

"The president's got time available during the day for whatever bilaterals he has in advance of the summit meeting with some of those attending. That has not been fully determined yet, but there will be at least two or three bilaterals," he said.
On Friday evening, a welcoming session is planned for the leaders at the governor's mansion in Denver. They will then have dinner at the University of Denver.

On Saturday, they will begin their deliberations at the Denver public library. That afternoon, the seven regular members of the group will meet without Yeltsin for about an hour to discuss economic issues, McCurry said.
He said dinner that night will be at a restaurant modelled after a mid-19th century southeastern Colorado trading post, which he said was known for serving buffalo, elk and beef.
Later, they will attend an evening of "uniquely American entertainment at the National Western Complex."
On Sunday, the leaders are expected to issue a final communique around midday and Clinton will give a news conference in the early afternoon.
